newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Unipetrol announces merger share swap plans.
newsitem.headline: Czech Unipetrol announces merger share swap plans.

text.p: The Czech petrochemical holding company Unipetrol a.s. said on Monday that it would submit a plan to shareholders calling for a swap at a ratio of 1.2 of its shares for each Kaucuk a.s. share, and 1.1 of its shares for each Chemopetrol a.s. share.

The plan, which would be submitted to the shareholders of all three companies at general meetings next month, completes a three-way merger joining the companies as one under the Unipetrol title, as part of the government's petrochemical privatisation plan.

"Shares of the existing Kaucuk group and Chemopetrol will be on the (Prague Stock Exchange) until the 30th of June when both companies should be eliminated from the business registry," Radomil Stepanek, a director at Unipetrol, told a news conference.
The swap would entail an exchange of 12 shares of Unipetrol, with a nominal value of 100 crowns each, with one Kaucuk share worth a nominal 1,000 crowns.
With Chemopetrol it would be 11 shares at a nominal 100 crowns for one 1,000 crown Chemopetrol share.
Unipetrol shares are still 100 percent held by the Czech government until the merger is complete.
Analysts do not expect public trading in Unipetrol shares until well after the deal is completed. Stepanek said a PSE listing could come as early as September.
All three companies plan general meetings to vote on the issue on March 27.
After the merger is complete, Unipetrol will have total combined equity of 18.13 billion crowns. The swap ratio is the result of an audit of the net commerical value of both Chemopetrol and Kaucuk.
Kaucuk shares traded 71 crowns higher on Monday's PSE fixing at 1,503, while Chemopetrol was up 82 crowns at 1,447 at the close of the real-time trading session at 1300 gmt.
The merger combines the non-refinery assets of Kaucuk and Chemopetrol under Unipetrol, after both refineries were combined in another company Ceska Rafinerska a.s. at the end of 1995.

Unipetrol controls fuels distribution company Benzina, as well as 51 percent of Ceska Rafinerska, created from the separating of the refining units from Chemopetrol and Kaucuk. A consortium of Conoco, Agip SpA , and Royal Dutch/Shell took a 49 percent stake in Rafinerska in 1995.
